name: Acalvaria

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Acalvaria

criteria.description: Congenital absence of the calvarial bones and scalp with preservation of the facial bones and brain tissue
Presence of normally developed cerebral cortex without major brain malformations
Intact dura mater underlying the absent calvarium
Prenatal ultrasound or MRI showing absent calvarial bones with normal brain parenchyma

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of congenital absence of calvarial bones and scalp with normal cerebral cortex on imaging
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily radiological and clinical; genetic testing is not definitive.

imaging: Prenatal ultrasound showing absent calvarial bones with normal brain tissue
MRI demonstrating absence of skull vault with preserved cerebral cortex and intact dura mater
genetic: No consistent genetic mutations identified; etiology remains unclear
other: Physical examination reveals absent scalp and skull over cerebral hemispheres

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of both brain and skull vault
Severe brain malformations and absence of cerebral hemispheres
Brain tissue exposed without skull coverage
Brain is malformed and degenerates over time
Multiple fractures and deformities, not isolated calvarial absence

redFlags: Absence of calvarial bones with exposed brain tissue
Neurological deterioration or seizures in neonate
Signs of infection or meningitis due to exposed brain
references: Pang D, et al. Acalvaria: clinical and radiological features. J Neurosurg Pediatr. 2010.
Prenatal diagnosis and management of acalvaria. Ultrasound Obstet Gynecol. 2015.
